episodes.210346: High winds developed across southern Lake Michigan during the morning of March 13th.
episodes.210394: From March 12th through March 14th of 2026, a large and powerful kona storm setup over the northern central Pacific, and brought numerous impacts across the state. This low was supported by a broad and potent upper level trough that lingered for many days. Impacts included flash flooding, wind damage, large surf, and strong thunderstorms.
episodes.210792: An strong upper-level low with an associated surface cold front allowed to ample lift in an environment with sufficient shear and instability for a line of showers and isolated thunderstorms to form during the afternoon and evening hours of March 13, 2026. Strong-to-damaging wind gusts were observed across northwestern Pennsylvania with these features with the most widespread wind damage in portions of Clearfield County during the late afternoon to early evening hours.
episodes.210820: An intense and prolonged atmospheric river (AR) impacted the Northern Rockies, directed primarily at North-Central Idaho. This event was characterized by a deep moisture plume and an unseasonably warm air mass, which transitioned mountain snow to a heavy rain-on-snow event. Total precipitation across the Clearwater Basin ranged from 2.5 to over 5.0 inches.  Impacts from this storm included power outages and impacts to travel.  The biggest impact, however, was flooding in Clearwater County near Orofino.  By the morning of March 13, several days of moderate rain and mild temperatures had completely saturated the soil. With the ground unable to absorb any more water and temperatures remaining above freezing overnight, continued rainfall and rapid snowmelt triggered immediate runoff. This surge of water overwhelmed culverts, destabilized hillsides, and caused rapid rises on small streams and the Clearwater River.
episodes.211669: A strong clipper low moving through the Upper Great Lakes brought strong winds to the area.  A few gusts to storm force were observed in northern Lake Michigan and the northern Bay of Green Bay.
episodes.212368: Rich tropical moisture south of a frontal boundary to the north of the area allowed for flooding from rainfall over portions of Southeast Florida.
episodes.212436: Strong low pressure system tracked across the region bringing storm force winds to Lake Michigan.
episodes.212441: Convective showers forming in advance of a passing cold front produced a family of three waterspouts offshore Plantation Key near Alligator Reef Light.

events.narrative: Heavy rain moved over southern Oahu in Honolulu and east Honolulu from the south. Flooding was reported on Queen Street and Kapiolani Boulevard. Landslides were reported on Diamond Head Road, the Punchbowl ramp onto the H1 west bound, and the Pali Highway ramp onto the H1 east bound. Flooding occurred on the H1 Pali offramp, and on Kalanianaole Highway. Significant erosion and undermining of Kalanianaole Highway caused total closure of the highway in both directions near Sealife Park. Nine homeless people and dog were rescued in the Manoa-Palolo Stream near Kaimuki High School due to rapidly rising stream levels. Pearl Highlands shopping center also had flooding.

Heavy rain led to road closures between Naalehu and Pahala due to a culvert overflowing. Highway 11 was also closed at Kawa Flats due to flooding. Then on March 14, water over Highway 11 cut off the towns on Naalehu and Pahala. The Department of Transportation reported Hawaii Belt Road (Route 11) at mile marker 57.5 at the Hilea Stream Bridge was closed due to flooding in the area.

On March 13, heavy rain began to fall and quickly led to extensive damage across  Maui. This damage included widespread infrastructure damage, property and home losses, and emergency rescues. At 1030 AM HST, heavy rain washed away Lower Kula Road near Ohala Place, and all of South Kihei Road closed due to severe flooding. On March 14, 40 people were reportedly stranded in Hana due to flooding. Honoapiilani Hwy (Hwy 30) was closed from  Kuihelani Hwy to the Olowalu dump due to flooding, swift water, and the integrity of  the Ukuhehame bridge. At approximately 3:45 pm on March 14, a section of South Kihei Road collapsed. Many other roads across Maui were also closed. A home in Iao Valley collapsed into the Iao River. A Target store in Kahului reported severe flooding with several inches of water inisde the store.

The most significant impact occurred south of Orofino, where a large landslide blocked US-12 between mile markers 44 and 45. The initial slide occurred around 1539MST on Friday, March 13. While crews worked to clear the route, a second slide occurred at the same location at 0920MST on Saturday, March 14. The highway remained closed in both directions until Saturday afternoon. Additional landslides and rockslides were reported on Lower Fords Creek Road, Grangemont Road, Sunnyside, and Bobbitt Bench. Heavy traffic diverted to Sunnyside Road caused that secondary route to begin failing under the saturated conditions.||In Orofino, the urban drainage system reached maximum capacity and overflowed, flooding residential areas. In the Riverside area (115th Street), rushing water surrounded homes and filled basements. Significant damage occurred at the Joint School District 171 bus garage when a nearby creek (likely Flume Creek) blew out, flooding the facility. While officials successfully moved most of the fleet, one school bus and a neighboring food pantry were inundated and suffered major damage.||Small streams and creeks, including Jim Fords Creek and Freeman Creek, crested their banks, threatening homes and washing out culverts. Near Weippe, a creek overflowed onto the roadway, causing significant rutting. The Clearwater River at Orofino saw a dramatic rise of over 8 feet, increasing from 5.78 feet on Thursday to a crest of 13.96 feet on Saturday night���staying just below the 16-foot flood stage, though the high water contributed to the drainage backup in the city. Total rainfall between March 10 and 15 included 3.57 in Orofino, 4.00 in Peck, and 4.50 at the Pierce SNOTEL.
